doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: Little George's playing style, lip and the WPA band
summary: Charlotte describes her brother's held notes, range, Dixieland and reading ability, and the last time his mother heard him with the WPA band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I know it's hard to describe a musician's style. But do you know. Did he play louder than most people? Or did he have a big song? Or high notes? Or anything about it like that? Oh, he used to hold notes.
Hold the real law. And my daughter. Yeah, what you can tell me about my son. Oh, yeah.

He traveled. And he was. He was. He was what you call. A voice class get off man. He could play all the Dixieland. Yeah. Any one of them. I mean. You know. It's called that in the Raid books. When you have the music up. You play a few numbers. A few orchestrations. And then you say. Let's get in the Raid books now. And the guitar. That's where they get to play all the Hayes numbers. So he was a master, man. He was. He just was a voice class drummer. How was his range?

Well, yeah. Well, he had a good lip. I mean. Yeah. A good lip. A tisimal lip. But he had a wonderful lip. Yeah. For the Raid that was trumpet. He had a wonderful lip. Mm-hmm. Wonderful. And I played brass band with him. You remember when they played the WPA band?
They came here. They played for them people from Washington. At the Hume Center one Sunday evening. That was the last time I heard little job play. Yeah.
And did he play that solo? I've seen his pictures ever left. Yeah. Yeah. That's right.

And did he play that solo? He was living right there on Russia. Yeah. He was one of trumpet players that you could open a book and knock it off. And yeah. I don't know it was on that page. Yeah. I don't know it was on that page. I don't know.
